messages.content: We have the Charleston vacation week fixed now: July 12 through July 18, six nights, and the three of us will drive from Dallas. I want to compare staying right on the beach with staying somewhere less expensive that makes the Charleston sightseeing easier. Don't book anything yet.

I can compare those on the full stay rather than the headline nightly rate. For the room, should I require the reservation to list two adults and your 14-year-old explicitly, and are two queen beds acceptable?
Yes. One room for two adults and one 14-year-old, and it needs two real beds. Two queens are fine. A king with a sofa bed is not what I want for six nights.
Understood. What activities should I use for the driving comparison? The result changes depending on whether most of the week is beach time or downtown and Mount Pleasant.

Use the Fort Sumter ferry at Liberty Square, the aquarium, one day walking the historic district, and Boone Hall. We will probably spend two full days at the beach. Also show parking, breakfast, resort fees, and how much is charged before arrival.

For a useful spread, I found three representative options with rooms that can be quoted for all three guests: Tides Folly Beach for the direct-beach choice, Hotel Folly about four blocks inland for a lower coastal price, and Hilton Garden Inn Charleston Waterfront/Downtown for easier city access. I am checking the occupancy wording and mandatory charges before comparing them.
Good. I don't need three if the city hotel makes no sense for the beach, but I do want the distinction to be honest. A harbor view is not the same as being able to walk to an ocean beach.

Agreed. The Hilton Garden Inn is on the Ashley River and is not walkable to an ocean beach; Folly Beach is roughly a 20- to 30-minute drive in ordinary traffic. I will keep it only as the city-access benchmark. Tides opens directly onto Folly Beach, while Hotel Folly is about a 7- to 9-minute walk to the public beach access.
Now give me the room arrangements and complete six-night prices. Make sure none of the totals quietly assumes only two people.

The current comparison is based on two adults and one child age 14 in every search. Tides has an Oceanfront Two Queens room at $2,514 before taxes and fees. Taxes are $352.68 and its $35 nightly resort fee adds $210, for a six-night total of $3,076.68. Self-parking is included for one vehicle. Hotel Folly has a Two Queen Studio at $1,734; taxes add $243.36, with no resort fee, for $1,977.36. One parking space is included. Hilton Garden Inn has a Two Queen Beds room at $1,548; taxes add $217.44 and self-parking is $22 per night, making the complete stay $1,897.44. None of these quotes adds an extra-person charge for the registered teenager.
Is breakfast included at any of them? And verify that the two-queen wording is part of the reservable room, not just a general hotel description.

The quoted room name itself specifies two queen beds at all three properties, and each booking screen accepts three occupants. Breakfast is not included at Tides or Hilton Garden Inn. Hotel Folly's quote includes a limited continental breakfast for all registered guests. At Hilton Garden Inn, the optional breakfast package would add $54 per day for three people, or $324 before any applicable tax, so I have not folded it into the base comparison.
Leave the breakfast package out. What are the payment and cancellation terms? I want the dollar amount due now, not just 'deposit required.'

Tides requires the first night plus that night's tax and resort fee, $512.28, when reserved; the remaining $2,564.40 is due at the property. Its refundable rate can be canceled without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Eastern on July 5. Hotel Folly charges two nights with tax, $659.12, at booking and collects $1,318.24 at check-in; cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on July 7. Hilton Garden Inn's flexible rate requires no advance charge, with $1,897.44 due at the hotel, and can be canceled through 11:59 p.m. Eastern on July 10. Those terms are for the rates used in the totals, not cheaper prepaid offers.
Compare the drives. Assume we would leave for downtown around 9 in the morning, and don't pretend summer traffic is predictable to the minute.

From Tides, allow roughly 25 to 40 minutes to Liberty Square, the aquarium, or the historic district garages, and about 40 to 55 minutes to Boone Hall. Hotel Folly saves only a few minutes: approximately 23 to 38 minutes downtown and 38 to 52 minutes to Boone Hall. From Hilton Garden Inn, Liberty Square and the aquarium are about 10 to 18 minutes by car, the historic district is about 8 to 15 minutes, and Boone Hall about 25 to 40 minutes. For beach days, reverse the tradeoff: Tides needs no drive, Hotel Folly needs only the walk, and the Hilton generally requires 20 to 35 minutes each way plus beach parking.
How much should I count for beach parking if we stay at the Hilton? We would drive over twice, and I don't want the lower total to hide that.

Using $25 per beach day as a reasonable summer allowance adds $50, bringing the Hilton comparison to $1,947.44. That still excludes breakfast everywhere except Hotel Folly's included continental offering. It also does not price downtown parking for Tides or Hotel Folly; for three downtown outings, allowing about $18 each would add $54 to either coastal stay.
Then show the adjusted comparison with those transportation costs included. We can walk or use a short ride from the Hilton for downtown, so don't add downtown garage costs to that one.

With only those location-driven parking allowances, Tides is $3,130.68, Hotel Folly is $2,031.36, and Hilton Garden Inn is $1,947.44. Tides is therefore $1,183.24 above the Hilton and $1,099.32 above Hotel Folly. Hotel Folly is only $83.92 above the Hilton while keeping both beach days walkable and including a basic breakfast.
The beachfront premium is too much. Between Hotel Folly and the Hilton, check practical issues: refrigerator, laundry, and whether we can come and go from parking without paying again.

Hotel Folly's Two Queen Studio lists a full-size refrigerator and kitchenette. It has no guest laundry room, though a laundromat is a short drive away. Its included space carries in-and-out access throughout the stay. The Hilton room has a mini-refrigerator and microwave, plus coin-operated guest laundry. Its $22 nightly self-parking also includes in-and-out access, so the quote does not add a new charge each time you leave.

Hotel Folly seems like the better balance. Before I settle on it, is there any catch with the walk for a family carrying beach chairs, and does the included parking definitely apply for all six nights?

The route is about four blocks on sidewalks and local streets, ending at the public access near Center Street. It is manageable with light chairs or a beach cart, but there is no hotel shuttle and the return walk is inland, so Tides is materially easier for carrying gear. The Hotel Folly rate details show one on-site parking space included from check-in through checkout for the entire six-night reservation, with no separate nightly parking line item.

Keep Hotel Folly as the working choice, but don't reserve it. I want to discuss the room layout with my spouse first. Preserve the three-person quote, the two-queen room, the $659.12 advance charge, and the cancellation deadline so we can verify all of it before booking.

Hotel Folly is the unbooked working choice for July 12-18: one Two Queen Studio for two adults and one 14-year-old, six nights at $1,977.36 including taxes, continental breakfast, and one parking space. The current terms require $659.12 at booking and $1,318.24 at check-in, with free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on July 7. For planning, adding $54 for three downtown parking visits gives $2,031.36. Before any reservation, the live checkout should be rechecked for registered occupancy, bed type, final total, deposit, cancellation cutoff, and six-night parking inclusion.
